grammar.title: Temporal Clauses & Frequency Adverbs in Gastrointestinal Assessment
grammar.title_uz: Gastroenterologik Anamnezda Vaqt Bog'lovchilari va Chastota Ravishlari
grammar.title_ru: Временные Предлоги и Наречия Частоты при Сборе Гастроэнтерологического Анамнеза
grammar.title_en: Temporal Clauses & Frequency Adverbs in Gastrointestinal Assessment
grammar.rule_explanation: Use temporal prepositions and clauses ('after eating', 'on an empty stomach', 'before bedtime') and frequency adverbs ('frequently', 'intermittently') to differentiate peptic vs duodenal vs gallbladder pain patterns.
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Oshqozon va o'n ikki barmoqli ichak yarasi hamda o't qopi og'riqlarini farqlashda vaqt bog'lovchilari ('after eating' - ovqatdan so'ng, 'on an empty stomach' - och qoringa) va chastota ravishlari ('frequently') juda muhim.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Временные конструкции ('after eating', 'on an empty stomach') и наречия частоты ('constantly') позволяют дифференцировать язву желудка, 12-перстной кишки и патологию желчного пузыря.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Temporal markers (after meals, on an empty stomach) correlate pain timing with gastric acid secretion and food intake.
grammar.structure_pattern: Does the burning pain occur + [before / after meals / on an empty stomach]?
grammar.structure_pattern_uz: Does the burning pain occur + [before / after meals / on an empty stomach]?
grammar.structure_pattern_ru: Does the burning pain occur + [before / after meals / on an empty stomach]?
grammar.structure_pattern_en: Does the burning pain occur before/after meals or on an empty stomach?

examples.translation_en: Evaluating postprandial dyspepsia and biliary pain.

examples.sentence: The gnawing stomach pain typically awakens me in the middle of the night on an empty stomach.
examples.translation_uz: Kemiruvchi oshqozon og'rig'i odatda meni yarim tunda, och qoringa uyg'otib yuboradi.
examples.translation_ru: Голодная ноющая боль в желудке обычно будит меня среди ночи натощак.
examples.translation_en: Classic duodenal ulcer pain timing description.

common_mistakes.incorrect: Pain happens when I will eat.
common_mistakes.correct: The pain happens when I eat.
common_mistakes.explanation_uz: Vaqt ergash gaplarda (when) kelasi zamon 'will' ishlatilmaydi, Present Simple qo'yiladi.
common_mistakes.explanation_ru: В придаточных времени с 'when' будущее время 'will' не употребляется — ставится Present Simple.
common_mistakes.explanation_en: Never use 'will' inside temporal clauses introduced by 'when' or 'after'.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: When were you first diagnosed with type 2 diabetes?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I was diagnosed three years ago during a routine health check. I wasn't experiencing obvious symptoms at the time.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: What treatment did you start after the diagnosis?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I started metformin and changed my diet. For a while, my glucose levels were fairly stable.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have your glucose readings changed recently?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. They've been considerably higher over the past month.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: When did you last check your blood glucose?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I checked it this morning before breakfast. It was 12.6 millimoles per litre. Nurse: His fasting capillary glucose here is 13.1 millimoles per litre.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you noticed increased thirst or urination?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I've been extremely thirsty and I've been getting up several times during the night to urinate.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: When did those symptoms begin?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: They started about two weeks ago.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you missed any doses of metformin recently?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I have. I missed several doses last week because I was working night shifts.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have your eating habits changed as well?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Unfortunately, yes. I've been eating more fast food and sweet snacks because I haven't had time to cook.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you ever had an HbA1c above your target?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. It was high six months ago, but it improved after I changed my diet.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you experienced vomiting, abdominal pain, marked weakness, or confusion?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: No vomiting or confusion, but I've been unusually tired.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: We need to repeat your HbA1c, check renal function and electrolytes, and assess whether your current treatment remains appropriate.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Does a high glucose reading mean that my medication has stopped working?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Not necessarily. Poor adherence, dietary changes, infection, stress, and progression of diabetes can all contribute to hyperglycemia. Nurse: I'll arrange the blood tests and record his current medications.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: If my HbA1c is very high, will I need insulin?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: It depends on the result and your overall clinical picture. We'll discuss the options once we have the full assessment.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I'm worried because I thought I was managing my diabetes well.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: The important thing is that you've come in now. We can identify what has changed and adjust the management rather than simply increasing medication without understanding the cause.

tests.question: Which of the following is the grammatically and clinically standard question to ask about the duration of symptoms?
tests.option_a: How long do you having this symptom?
tests.option_b: How long has this condition been bothering you?
tests.option_c: Since what time you have this problem?
tests.option_d: How many days you are feeling pain?
tests.explanation: Klinik anamnezda davomiylikni so'rash uchun Present Perfect Continuous ('How long has... been bothering you?') to'g'ri shakl hisoblanadi.

tests.question: When evaluating acute pain, what is the best phrasing to assess pain character?
tests.option_a: Is your pain bad or very bad?
tests.option_b: Can you describe the pain—is it sharp, dull, throbbing, or aching?
tests.option_c: Why do you have sharp pain today?
tests.explanation: Og'riq xarakterini aniqlashda shifokor ochiq va taklif qiluvchi variantlar (sharp, dull, throbbing, aching) beradi.
